eyebrow: Morning Brief · Pre-market ~5am ET · Wed Jun 24
headline: The AI selloff goes global — but the plumbing still holds.
stance: A second day of AI/semiconductor selling has spread overseas — Korea's Kospi fell 10% — yet credit, funding and bond-market volatility stay calm. The engine holds Risk On · Neutral; tonight's Micron earnings are the real test of the AI-spending story.

news.head: Global tech selloff
news.body: Korea's Kospi fell 10% Tuesday (SK Hynix, Samsung each −12%+); European chip names (STMicro, ASMI) −7%+. The AI-spending-payoff question has gone global.

news.head: Yen weakness accelerating
news.body: USD/JPY is approaching 162 overnight — the yen near a 3-year low; Bank of Japan intervention risk is real and rising.

news.head: Today's calendar
news.body: May new home sales (10am ET), the Fed's annual bank stress-test results (4:30pm ET), and Micron (MU) earnings after the close.

implications: The selloff is concentrated in AI/semis while credit and funding stay calm — no systemic signal yet, but two straight days of sharp tech losses with global spillover is a yellow flag.
Washed-out equity positioning limits panic-selling, but Micron tonight is the key re-rating event for the whole AI-capex narrative.
The yen at a 3-year extreme keeps Bank of Japan intervention risk live — a sudden move would hit dollar crosses fast and broadly.
Copper speculators are piled into longs at a 3-year high — a contrarian warning; don't chase copper here.

watch.head: Micron (MU) earnings, after the close
watch.body: the market's verdict on AI memory demand — a miss reprices the sector, a beat could reverse Tuesday's damage.

watch.head: Fed bank stress-test results, 4:30pm ET
watch.body: any surprise failures would pressure bank stocks and credit spreads.

watch.head: May new home sales, 10am ET
watch.body: an affordability test with the 10-year at 4.50%.

watch.head: USD/JPY above 162
watch.body: watch for Bank of Japan verbal warnings or unannounced intervention.

watch.head: The open
watch.body: S&P futures are up pre-market — do buyers hold, or do sellers re-emerge?

sections.title: Macro & Rates
sections.prose: The 10-year closed at 4.50% and the 2-year at 4.16% (both prior close, Jun 23); the curve is faintly positive at +34bp. The real, inflation-adjusted yield sits at 2.29% — still a genuine drag on risk assets. The dollar index closed 101.39 Tuesday and is at 2026 highs overnight on yen weakness, with USD/JPY at 161.52, the yen's weakest in nearly three years. The MOVE index — the bond market's volatility gauge — is 68.8: bond traders are calm.
sections.positioning: Speculators in short-term-rate futures have almost no bullish bets left — the most washed-out in three years; the market may be too pessimistic about rate relief.

sections.title: Equity Markets
sections.prose: The S&P 500 closed at 7,365 (−1.44%) Tuesday, the Nasdaq 100 at 25,587 (−2.21%), the Dow at 51,667 (−0.09%); S&P futures point to a modestly higher open. AI/semiconductor names led the selling — Micron and Sandisk each fell 13%+ on doubts that big-tech AI-infrastructure spending will earn its return. Valuations stay rich (CAPE 40.96) and breadth is mediocre — under 60% of the S&P sits above its 200-day average.
sections.positioning: Speculators in S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Russell 2000 futures all have almost no bullish bets left (2nd–10th percentile over three years) — a contrarian floor that limits panic-selling, not a timing call.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
sections.prose: Investment-grade spreads are 74bp over Treasuries and the high-yield premium 265bp — tight, no stress. Short-term funding shows no strain, bank reserves are ample at $3,033bn, and overnight Fed facility usage is near zero ($6.5bn) — excess cash has largely drained from the system. No distress is leaking from the equity selloff.
sections.positioning: Primary dealers are sitting on their largest high-yield inventory in three years — if sentiment sours, that supply could hit the market quickly.

single_name.note: (Radian Group, a mortgage insurer) — insiders buying alongside large off-exchange block buys and unusual options activity, with light short interest. Fits the credit/financial theme into tonight's stress tests.
